title: Steam explosion‐assisted extraction, structure characterization, gastrointestinal distribution and gut microbiota modulation of polysaccharide from Gracilaria lemaneiformis
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Gracilaria lemaneiformis is a marine red alga with potential biological and prebiotic activities. We hypothesized that steam explosion pretreatment has the potential to disrupt the cell wall structure of G. lemaneiformis, promote polysaccharide release, and affect the gut microbiota modulation of polysaccharide from G. lemaneiformis.

RESULTS

In this work, steam explosion was applied to prepare G. lemaneiformis polysaccharide (GLPS), and its extraction efficiency, structural characteristics, gastrointestinal distribution, and microbiota modulation were investigated. Here, the yield of crude polysaccharide (based on dry weight) from G. lemaneiformis was improved to 508.2 ± 4.0 g kg−1 by steam explosion pretreatment, which was 1.61-fold higher than the controls. GLPS is a heteropolysaccharide with a molecular weight of 1.399 × 106 Da, and is composed of galactose (89.23%), glucose (6.30%), xylose (2.90%) and glucuronic acid (1.57%). In addition, fluorescence imaging results indicate that Sulfo-Cyanine5.5 amine-labeled GLPS was mainly distributed in the stomach and small intestine at 1–3 h, and gradually reached the large intestine after digestion for 3 h. Furthermore, GLPS increased the relative abundance of beneficial bacteria, including Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group (P = 0.0327), Alistipes (P = 0.0151), norank_f__Lachnospiraceae (P = 0.0169), and Rikenella (P = 0.0198). It is remarkable that GLPS enhanced the level of butyric acid, which was 2.87-fold higher than the controls.

CONCLUSION

Steam explosion pretreatment improved the extraction efficiency of GLPS, which exhibited potential gut microbiota regulatory activity, providing a theoretical basis for the high-value utilization of marine algal polysaccharides. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
